newsitem.title: UK: CP Ships expects Lykes takeover decision in weeks.
newsitem.headline: CP Ships expects Lykes takeover decision in weeks.

text.p: CP Ships said on Wednesday that it expected to hear from U.S. authorities within two weeks on whether it can go ahead with its $34 million takeover bid for the container shipping services of Florida-based Lykes Lines.
Canadian Pacific Ltd chairman and president David O'Brien said: "We are awaiting a decision on our takeover of Lykes from the U.S. Maritime Authority, Marad, within the next two weeks."
Marad's agreement to the takeover is required because Lykes Lines' vessel are U.S.-flagged and therefore available for military call-up, he said.
"All the commercial arrangements are already agreed," O'Brien added, "and although the indications are good, the Marad decision involves Washington politics and we can only wait to hear."
O'Brien said: "With the addition of Lykes, our CP Ships' revenues should rise 50 percent to over Canadian $1.5 billion."

He added the acquisition of the U.S. shipping line, which is currently under Chapter 11 protection, would give CP Ships "a broader market coverage in the U.S. and an even stronger strategic position on the North Atlantic."
CP Ships acquired Atlantic container operator Cast in 1995 when it was insolvent. Since then Cast has reported a 15 percent growth in shipments.
In 1996 CP Ships' container volumes increased by 20 percent to 480,000 teus (twenty foot equivalent units) as revenues rose 18 percent to $1.1 billion, O'Brien added.
"In about 10 years, we have become both the highest volume and lowest cost operator on the North Atlantic between Europe and North America," he said.

O'Brien said much of CP Ships' growth was based on a concentration of its services on the port of Montreal which gave a gateway closer to the centre of the north American industrial heartland around Chicago than rival ports.

"Concentrating a large part of its business on one rail operator also gives a cost advantage," he said of CP Ships ability to utilise synergies with group company Canadian Pacific Railway. -- Paul Berrill, Reuters Shipping News + Tel 44 171 542 4087
